summary: 71-year-old woman brought in drowsy and confused with 5 days of vomiting and abdominal pain: adjusted calcium 3.84 mmol/L, PTH 38 pmol/L, creatinine 196. Hypercalcaemic crisis: emergency IV 0.9% saline, IV bisphosphonate after rehydration, stop contributing drugs, cardiac monitoring; parathyroidectomy once stable.

inputs.hpi: Daughter reports 5 days of vomiting, constipation, vague abdominal pain and increasing thirst; confused and drowsy since yesterday. Takes bendroflumethiazide and calcium/vitamin D tablets. Known "slightly high calcium" 3 years ago, not followed up.

exam.general: Drowsy (responds to voice), GCS 13, dry mucous membranes. Pulse 104, BP 102/60.
exam.abdomen: Soft, mild diffuse tenderness, no peritonism.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Hypercalcaemic crisis due to primary hyperparathyroidism with acute kidney injury
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Hypercalcaemic crisis (adjusted Ca 3.84) from primary hyperparathyroidism (PTH 38) with AKI and reduced consciousness. IV 0.9% saline, then IV bisphosphonate; stop thiazide and calcium/vitamin D; cardiac monitoring; HDU; urgent parathyroidectomy when stable (consider parathyroid carcinoma).

mustInclude.note: Thiazide and calcium/vitamin D supplements must be stopped.

mustExclude.note: A parathyroid patient's documented plan must not contain a thyroidectomy operation or lifelong levothyroxine (wrong operation in the record).
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Same dx-variant substring bug: the crisis plan opens with the elective Total Thyroidectomy template.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Add a Parathyroid dx-variant group ahead of Thyroid; word-boundary matching.

mustExclude.note: Loop diuretics only after rehydration (or for fluid overload).

guideline.name: Society for Endocrinology emergency guidance — acute hypercalcaemia in adults
guideline.section: Severe or symptomatic hypercalcaemia: IV 0.9% saline rehydration, IV bisphosphonate after rehydration, stop contributing drugs, monitor renal function
guideline.citation: Walsh J, Gittoes N, Selby P; Society for Endocrinology Clinical Committee. Society for Endocrinology Endocrine Emergency Guidance: Emergency management of acute hypercalcaemia in adult patients. Endocr Connect. 2016;5:G9–G11.

guideline.name: Fifth International Workshop — evaluation and management of primary hyperparathyroidism
guideline.section: Diagnosis (PTH, exclude FHH, vitamin D); surgical indications (serum calcium >0.25 mmol/L above ULN, osteoporosis T-score ≤−2.5 or vertebral fracture, eGFR <60 mL/min, nephrolithiasis/nephrocalcinosis, hypercalciuria, age <50); localisation only once surgery is decided
guideline.citation: Bilezikian JP, Khan AA, Silverberg SJ, et al. Evaluation and management of primary hyperparathyroidism: summary statement and guidelines from the Fifth International Workshop. J Bone Miner Res. 2022;37:2293–2314.

rationale: Permutation: metabolic emergency. Reduced consciousness (AVPU V), AKI, vomiting. Tests emergency escalation from labs and the drug-stopping step.
